This is an email thread with (email hidden), subject "RMA Shop····".

What has been said so far:
Customer: This was delivered Jul 10th Shop····. I have a Voltage Protection Error on the display. I tried rebooting it several times. [image: IMG_2973.jpeg] Thanks, T.J. S.
You: Hi T.J., Thanks for the photo, it tells me a lot. Your board is on the network (phone hidden), wifi connected), the BM1370 side is detected, the temperature is a cold 32 C and the power reads 0.062 W with 0.0 GH/s. That means the miner is powering up fine but the firmware is cutting the ASIC core rail straight away and showing the protection screen, so it never gets to hash. A reboot will not clear that on its own, which matches what you are seeing. On the code itself I want to be straight with you: #···· is not documented in the firmware release notes or the public issue tracker, and I wi
Customer: I’m running a 350 Meanwell PSU. I tried another one with the same issue so it’s not the PSU. I’ll try to flash the FW and try again. I’ll repot back tomorrow. Thanks, T.J. S. On W., Oct 21, 2026 at 8:17 PM Hal — HeliumDeploy Support < (email hidden)> wrote:
You: Hi T.J., Good, that is the most useful thing you could have told me. A Meanwell 350 is plenty of supply, and a second one behaving the same way takes the power source off the list, so whatever is cutting the core rail is on the board or in the firmware. For the flash, use the flasher at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, pick the NerdQaxe++ profile, and do the factory image with a full erase rather than the over the air update. The factory route writes from the start of flash and wipes saved settings, which is exactly what you want here, since a half written image or a stored frequency and volta
Customer: I loaded the Harlolabs OS, I only see this for rev 6.1. Is this correct one? [image: image.png] Thanks, T.J. S. On W., Oct 21, 2026 at 8:50 PM Hal — HeliumDeploy Support < (email hidden)> wrote:
You: Hi T.J., Yes, I opened your screenshot: the list shows NERDOCTAXE REV3, NERDQAXE REV5, NERDQAXE REV6 (highlighted), NerdQaxe++ Rev.7 and NEXUS L1. For a Rev 6.1 unit the right entry is NERDQAXE REV6. There is no separate 6.1 image, because 6.1 is a small spin of the rev6 board and it runs the same profile. Please do not pick NerdQaxe++ Rev.7. Rev7 is a different board with a different power stage (the upstream project lists rev7 separately as the TPS546 board, which is why it has its own entry), and a rev7 image on a rev6 board can set the core rail up wrongly, which is the last thing we want 
Customer: I already flashed it. But it is a NerdQAxe++ 6.1. this is what i see in log [image: image.png] [image: image.png] Thanks, T.J. S. On W., Oct 21, 2026 at 10:01 PM Hal — HeliumDeploy Support < (email hidden)> wrote:
You: Hi T.J., That is the unit coming back to life. I opened both screenshots. The log line that matters is the pair: "NerdQaxe++ Rev6.1 controller map matched; ASIC rails are off" and then, a fraction of a second later, "ASIC rails enabled at 1150 mV per domain", followed by BM1370 chips 1, 2, 3 and 4 detected and a chip count of 4. On the old firmware the rails were being cut and never came back, which is what put the protection screen up. Now they come up and stay up, and all four chips enumerate. So this was firmware, not the board and not your Meanwell. A few things on the dashboard so you kno
Customer: The Harlo OS would never mine shares. I wiped the ROM using ESP Tool and loaded NerdQAxe OS back and have the same issue. [image: image.png] Thanks, T.J. S. On W., Oct 21, 2026 at 10:16 PM Hal — HeliumDeploy Support < (email hidden)> wrote:
You: Hi T.J., Thanks for going all the way through that, including the full esptool wipe. I opened the new log and it is the clearest evidence we have had. Two lines tell the story. The regulator reports TPS536X7_status with word 8841 and vout 10, which is a latched undervoltage fault on the core output with power good dropped and the converter switched off, and the input status is clean at 00. The line underneath confirms it from the other side: vin 12.06 V, so your Meanwell is delivering exactly what it should, but vout 0.00, iout 0.00 and pout 0.00, with the regulator sitting cold at 19.75 C and
Customer: It used to have a white sticker on the back of the board, not sure where it has went. Thanks, T.J. S. On Thu, Oct 22, 2026 at 8:27 AM Hal — HeliumDeploy Support < (email hidden)> wrote:
You: Hi T.J., No problem, that sticker goes missing often enough and it does not hold anything up. We can identify the unit other ways. If the board is still powered up and reachable, the easiest substitute is the network identity the firmware reports. Open the web UI and note the MAC address and the hostname it shows, plus the firmware version and the board version it reports (501 for your Rev 6.1). Those three together pin the board down. If you would rather not power it again, a plain photo of the back of the board showing the empty sticker area and any numbers printed in the silkscreen works to

Their latest email, the one you are answering now:
I have not seen anyone reply to this?

Thanks,
T.J. S.

On Thu, Oct 22, 2026 at 8:51 AM Hal — HeliumDeploy Support <
(email hidden)> wrote:

Hi T.J.,

You have not been forgotten, and nothing is waiting on you right now.

Here is where things stand. The last log you sent settled it: the core regulator is latching an undervoltage fault with the input clean at 12.06 V and the output at 0.00 V, and that held true across two power supplies, a full Harlo OS factory flash and a complete esptool erase back to NerdQaxe OS. That is a board level fault on the power stage, not firmware, not your Meanwell and not a setting. I have passed those findings, along with the logs and photos you sent, to our hardware team as a return for the Rev 6.1 unit on Shop····.

That return is with the team for review now. They are offline until 10am Eastern today, and they pick it up from there, so you should have their confirmation by email in this same thread. The missing white sticker does not hold it up, and you do not need to do anything further with the unit in the meantime. Please leave it unplugged rather than retrying it, since the regulator is faulted and more power cycles will not change anything.

If you want to compare notes with other NerdQaxe owners while you wait, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is there as @nullhashrate.

Thanks for your patience through all that testing, it is what made the diagnosis clear.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Support
